body: Flag: MIXED. Airports-energy-infrastructure group (Delhi and Hyderabad airports; Goa, overseas airports). Survived a 2013-2020 leverage crisis via asset sales and strategic equity (Tata-GIC-SSG 2019 deal, Groupe ADP buying 49% of GMR Airports Ltd for ~Rs 10,780 cr in 2020). Restructuring: 2021 demerger of non-airport businesses (energy, urban infra, EPC) into GMR Power & Urban Infra (GPUIL), leaving GMR Airports Infrastructure (GIL) as an airport pure-play; 2024 merger of GIL with unlisted GMR Airports Ltd to simplify the structure and settle most GPUIL-related contingent liabilities. Minority concerns: long history of the listed holdco supporting loss-making energy subsidiaries through loans/guarantees; complex multi-layer structure with holdco discount; persistently high promoter encumbrance -- an aggregator summary of a Nov-2025 filing put ~50.6% of promoter shares in GPUIL as encumbered (verify on NSE SAST). No SEBI/ED fraud findings against the promoters were found in this scan; the Maldives airport cancellation (2012) and Indonesian coal assets were capital-allocation losses. Positives: airport-business value has been preserved and grown; strategic partners came in at arm's length prices; promoter has not been accused of siphoning. Status Nov-2026: GIL is the main listed vehicle; watch encumbrance, RPT approvals between GPUIL and GIL, and dilution via preferential/ convertible issues to partners.

data.good_conduct: demerger 2021; merger 2024 simplification; strategic equity at arm's length
data.red_flags: high encumbrance at GPUIL; inter-group support for energy losses; layered holdcos

title: GMR group (G.M. Rao family) — governance history
